title: Launch Workload Dashboard
description: Verifies GCP authentication, resolves cluster, project, TPU generation, and backing reservations for a target workload, seeds the dashboard configuration, ensures the local dashboard server is running, generates a direct deep-linked URL focusing on the workload, and verifies that URL resolves and stays responsive during the scan before reporting it.

step_notes.gcloud-login: Ensures active gcloud CLI authentication and Application Default Credentials (ADC) are valid before API queries.
step_notes.validate-workload: Verifies workload initialization and recovers the underlying cluster name, GCP project ID, and regional location from audit and runtime logs.
step_notes.resolve-cluster-metadata: Inspects the target GKE cluster to resolve TPU generation (e.g. tpu7x, v6e, v5p) and backing GCE reservation before dashboard provisioning.
step_notes.configure-and-launch-dashboard: Provisions the cluster with full metadata in clusters_config.json, launches or verifies the dashboard server daemon, triggers a scan, and returns the deep-linked URL. Returns server_status UNRESPONSIVE (not START_TIMEOUT) when a hung server still holds the port; stop that process before retrying.
step_notes.verify-dashboard-url: Never report a dashboard URL that has not passed this step (url_status VERIFIED, or DEGRADED with a latency caveat). Probes DNS plus the page and /api/health repeatedly while the scan runs, because a server can pass one health check and then freeze once the scan spawns gcloud/kubectl. UNRESOLVABLE: rerun with --hostname localhost. DOWN: nothing listening; relaunch. UNRESPONSIVE: follow url_hint (GRPC_ENABLE_FORK_SUPPORT=0 in _dashboard/server.py, SCAN_CLUSTER_WORKERS), restart the server, and rerun this step.
